title: Triples with Bitwise AND Equal To Zero
description:
# Triples with Bitwise AND Equal To Zero

Given an integer array `nums`, return the number of ordered triples `(i, j, k)` such that:

`nums[i] & nums[j] & nums[k] == 0`

The triple is ordered, so `(i, j, k)` and `(j, i, k)` are different when the indices differ. The same index may also be used more than once.

`&` is bitwise AND: an output bit is `1` only when all corresponding input bits are `1`; otherwise it is `0`.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [2,1,3]
**Output:** 12
**Explanation:** There are 12 ordered triples whose bitwise AND is 0.

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [0,0,0]
**Output:** 27
**Explanation:** Every ordered triple is valid because every selected value is 0.

## Constraints:

* `1 <= nums.length <= 1000`
* `0 <= nums[i] < 2^16`

solutions.name: Dense Pairwise AND Frequency Scan
solutions.description:
## Approach
Precompute `pairCount[mask]`, the number of ordered pairs `(i, j)` with `nums[i] & nums[j] == mask`. Then for every third value `c`, scan all masks and add the pair counts whose mask is disjoint from `c`.

## Key Insight
The condition can be grouped as `(nums[i] & nums[j]) & nums[k] == 0`. Once pair AND results are counted, each third value only needs to know which pair masks have no common set bit with it.

## Complexity Analysis
There are O(n^2) ordered pairs and 2^16 possible masks. The time complexity is O(n^2 + n * 2^16), and the space complexity is O(2^16).

solutions.name: Frequency-Compressed Pair Masks
solutions.description:
## Approach
First count how often each distinct number appears. Build pair-mask frequencies by iterating over distinct values instead of raw indices, multiplying their frequencies to preserve ordered pair counts. Then scan those pair masks for each third value.

## Key Insight
Many inputs contain duplicates. If value `a` appears `fa` times and value `b` appears `fb` times, then ordered pairs using those values contribute `fa * fb` to mask `a & b`.

## Complexity Analysis
Let `u` be the number of distinct values and `m` the number of distinct pair AND masks. The time complexity is O(u^2 + n * m), and the space complexity is O(u + m).

solutions.name: Complement Submask Enumeration
solutions.description:
## Approach
Count ordered pair AND masks in an array. For each third value `c`, valid pair masks must be submasks of `FULL_MASK ^ c`. Enumerate exactly those submasks and add their pair counts.

## Key Insight
A mask `p` satisfies `(p & c) == 0` if and only if all set bits of `p` lie inside the zero-bit positions of `c`. Those masks are precisely the submasks of `~c` within 16 bits.

## Complexity Analysis
Pair counting costs O(n^2). The query cost depends on the number of zero bits in each third value. The space complexity is O(2^16).

solutions.name: Subset Zeta Transform Query Table
solutions.description:
## Approach
After counting ordered pair AND masks, run a subset zeta transform so `subsetSum[mask]` stores the total count of pair masks that are submasks of `mask`. Then each third value `c` answers in O(1) by querying `subsetSum[FULL_MASK ^ c]`.

## Key Insight
The same complement-submask query is repeated for many values. The zeta transform precomputes every possible submask sum once, turning each triple query into a table lookup.

## Complexity Analysis
Pair counting is O(n^2), the transform is O(16 * 2^16), and the final scan is O(n). Space complexity is O(2^16).

solutions.name: Bitwise Trie over Pair Masks
solutions.description:
## Approach
Insert every ordered pair AND mask into a binary trie. To query a third value `c`, walk the trie bit by bit: if `c` has a 1 bit, the pair mask must have 0 there; if `c` has a 0 bit, both pair-mask branches are allowed.

## Key Insight
The trie encodes the same disjoint-mask predicate as a constrained bit traversal. It is useful as a teaching route because it makes the per-bit compatibility condition explicit.

## Complexity Analysis
Each ordered pair insertion touches 16 bits, and each query touches at most both compatible branches across 16 levels. The time complexity is O(n^2 * 16 + n * 16) in the compressed trie model, and the space complexity is O(n^2 * 16) in the worst case.
